title: Douglas Crockford and the Naming of JSON (early 2000s)
explainer: JSON - the format you'll likely reach for when a config file needs to be read by tools written in several different languages at once - wasn't designed from scratch for that purpose. Douglas Crockford noticed that a JavaScript-style object-literal syntax was already being used informally for data exchange, and around 2001, with Chip Morningstar, he specified, named, and popularized it as its own language-independent format. That history is exactly why JSON reads equally naturally from Python, JavaScript, or almost any other language in a polyglot repo: it was deliberately stripped down to syntax that family of languages already shares.
